test_title: PYST 66: RRB Group D - GA (Held On: 26 Dec, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: According to the Union Budget 2025-26, how much borrowing is planned to be raised through gross market borrowing in the financial year 2025-26?
solution:
The correct answer is __**₹14.82 lakh crore**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Union Budget 2025-26** was presented by the **Union Minister for Finance and Corporate Affairs**, **Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman**, in **Parliament** on **February 1, 2025**.
 
• According to the budget estimates, the **gross market borrowing** through dated securities for the financial year **2025-26** is planned at **₹14.82 lakh crore**.
 
• This borrowing is part of the government's strategy to finance the **Fiscal Deficit** while ensuring that the **private sector** has enough space for credit as the economy grows.
 
• The **net market borrowing** for the same period (FY 2025-26) is estimated to be **₹11.23 lakh crore**, which is the amount borrowed after accounting for the repayment of past loans.
 
• The fiscal deficit for **2025-26** is estimated at **4.3%** of the **Gross Domestic Product (GDP)**, showing a continued commitment to the **fiscal consolidation glide path**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Capital Expenditure (Capex):**

 
 
• The **Capital Expenditure** outlay for **2025-26** has been increased to **₹12.01 lakh crore**.
 
• This represents a significant portion of the total budget, aimed at boosting **infrastructure**, **logistics**, and **industrial growth** across the **country**.
 
• Higher Capex is expected to have a **multiplier effect** on the **economy**, creating **employment** and improving long-term productivity.
 
 
 
• **Total Expenditure and Receipts:**
 
 
• The **total expenditure** for the financial year **2025-26** is estimated at **₹53.07 lakh crore**.
 
• The **total receipts** (other than borrowings) are estimated at **₹34.40 lakh crore**.
 
• The **Gross Tax Revenue** is expected to see steady growth, driven by **GST (Goods and Services Tax)**, **Direct Taxes**, and **Corporate Taxes**.
 
 
 
• **Fiscal Consolidation:**
 
 
• The government aims to reach a **fiscal deficit** level below **4.5%** by the year **2025-26**.
 
• By targeting **4.3%** in this budget, the government is successfully adhering to the **Medium-Term Fiscal Policy** framework.
 
• Managing **market borrowings** effectively is crucial to maintain **macroeconomic stability** and keep **inflation** within the target range set by the **RBI (Reserve Bank of India)**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Market Borrowing Mechanism:** The **Government of India** borrows from the domestic market by issuing **Dated Securities** and **Treasury Bills**. The **RBI** acts as the investment manager for the government.
 
• **Dated Securities:** These are long-term **debt instruments** that carry a fixed or floating **coupon rate** (interest rate) paid on the face value, with a **tenure** ranging from **5 years to 40 years**.
 
• **Significance of the Figures:** The planned **₹14.82 lakh crore** gross borrowing is manageable and was well-received by the **bond market**, as it indicates that the government is not over-leveraging despite high **expenditure** needs.
 
• **Comparison:** In the **Interim Budget 2024-25**, the gross borrowing was pegged at **₹14.13 lakh crore**, showing a marginal and calibrated increase for the **2025-26** full budget to support **developmental goals**.
